newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FLOODS MOVE DOWNSTREAM, STABILISING UPSTREAM.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FLOODS MOVE DOWNSTREAM, STABILISING UPSTREAM.

text.p: The worst Czech flooding this century, covering much of the eastern part of the country, moved down river to the southeast on Thursday, while easing in the northern part of the region, officials said.
Scores of soldiers, firemen and rescuers continued to evacuate thousands of people on Thursday from towns and villages further downstream on the Morava and Opava rivers.
The disaster has claimed at least 17 lives, the local news agency CTK said, while dozens have been reported missing in the Czech Republic.
The floods have also hit parts of neighbouring Poland, Slovakia and Austria. Polish radio reported that at least 15 people had died in Poland as a result of the floods.

"It seems that the situation is improving... (levels of) upper streams of rivers are going down in number of towns there are declines in the range of three or four metres," Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told reporters during an extraordinary cabinet meeting dealing with the situation.
Klaus said the main flood wave was moving south, and that the culmination of the worst floowing on the Morava river in south was expected on Thursday night and Friday morning.
The floods, induced by heavy rains earlier this week which ended on Wednesday, have forced tens of thousands out of their homes in villages, towns, and cities.
Many houses have been swept away and tens of thousands of have been reported as damaged.
CTK said 100 square kilometres were flooded just in the area around the town of Kromeriz.
Major cities have been inundated, including parts of the 326,000-resident industrial city of Ostrava, and the whole of the city of Olomouc with over 100,000 residents.
Klaus said the cabinet agreed to dispatch 5,000 more soldiers in the flooded Czech territory to allay fears of homes being looted during the evacutations.
He said thousands of military service reserves would be mobilised to work in the affected areas, and unemployed citizens would be invited to take part in renewal works.
Army water tanks have been sent to the worst-affected regions, enabling supply of as much as 200,000 people with five litres of potable water per day, Klaus said.

He said that there was no shortage of food, water or fuel apart form temporary delays caused by transportation of relief supplies. He said the cabinet would take steps to fight price gouging of basic commodities.
Some 70,000 phone lines have been cut as well as electricity supplies, rail and road connection to parts of the region has been suspended.
Total damage on private property, infrastructure and fields has been estimated in the tens of billions of crowns.
Many industrial companies, including some of the country's largest exporters such as Volskwagens AG Czech unit Skoda Automobilova a.s., have been forced to close down or restrict production.
